definition: Umbrage means offense or resentment at a slight.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word umbrage. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know umbrage should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: She took umbrage at being seated by the kitchen doors and spent the whole dinner radiating polite frost.
Pique is a flash of wounded pride, gone by dessert — lighter than umbrage, which settles in and stays the evening.
Outrage goes further than umbrage: a public roar of anger, where umbrage smolders at a personal slight.

Offense is the everyday, all-purpose word for feeling insulted, and it says nothing about size or duration. Umbrage is offense in formal dress: taken at a slight, worn where others can see it, and nursed a while. Anyone gives offense; umbrage must be taken.

Resentment is a longer-simmering sense of unfair treatment — it can build for months over pay, chores, or credit. Umbrage arrives all at once, at one identifiable slight, and is usually visible on the spot. Resentment accumulates quietly; umbrage is taken, publicly, at something.

Indignation is offense with a righteous edge — anger that a rule of fairness has been broken, often on someone else's behalf. Umbrage is more personal and smaller: wounded dignity at a slight to oneself. The indignant cite a principle; those taking umbrage cite the insult to themselves.

For forty years Harold Pruitt's hardware store had anchored the Founders' Day parade, his flatbed of antique tools rolling directly behind the mayor.
This year the printed lineup put him ninth, behind a smoothie franchise.
Harold read the sheet twice at the counter, folded it, and took umbrage in full view of six customers.
He simply wore the insult like a boutonniere: a stiff nod for the parade chairman, regrets sent to the pancake breakfast, his famous window display gone dark for the week.
It was not the town he was angry with, and no great principle was at stake.
It was one slight, to him, and everyone was allowed to see exactly what he thought of it.
Forty years of goodwill, the barber observed, and one line of type had undone it — for exactly as long as Harold chose to be seen minding.
